newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yamaichi Int to limit dealings with Daiwa, Nikko.
newsitem.headline: Yamaichi Int to limit dealings with Daiwa, Nikko.

text.p: Yamaichi International Capital Management Co Ltd said on Wednesday it would limit its stock and bond dealings with Daiwa Securities Co Ltd and Nikko Securities Co Ltd.
"Limiting deals means that when we can conduct transactions through other companies, we will try not to conduct deals with Daiwa and Nikko," an official of Yamaichi International Capital said.
The company is likely to conduct fewer deals with the two securities houses, the official said.
Yamaichi International Capital decided on the move following media reports that Daiwa and Nikko had conducted illicit stock trades for a "sokaiya" racketeer, the official said.
He added, however, that the company did not know if the reports were true.

Earlier on Wednesday, the capital management firm said that it had halted stock and bond transactions through Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd after prosecutors raided Yamaichi Securities looking for evidence of suspected illegal stock deals.
The company has suspended transactions through Nomura Securities Co Ltd since March, the company official said. Nomura, Japan's largest brokerage, has been at the heart of a racketeer payoff scandal.
"Even if we halt transactions through all four securities companies, that would not adversely affect our business as there are many other good securities houses," the company official said.
The four securities houses, known as the "Big Four", are Japan's top brokerages.
Yamaichi International Capital Management is five-percent owned by Yamaichi Securities. The remaining 95 percent is held by other firms in the Yamaichi Securities group.
